subject: Clarification on SOC 2 Type II coverage, hosting jurisdiction, and bridge letter
messages:
From: Daniela Gomez <daniela.gomez@havenbank.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: security-team@havenbank.com
Date: 2026-08-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: SOC 2 Type II report and hosting / dataflow questions

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we progress to procurement we need a couple of confirmations for our security review:

1) Can you provide your latest SOC 2 Type II report and confirm the audit period that it covers? HavenBank needs coverage that overlaps Q1 2026.
2) We need a short bridge letter if the report end date is before contract signing, describing controls continuity until execution.
3) Hosting / dataflow: does any production customer data or KV cache leave the EU for processing (control plane, monitoring, backups)? If so, please list where and under what legal basis (SCCs, adequacy, or explicit consent).
4) Are there any cross-border subprocessors relevant to our instance?

We can take redacted files if necessary. Also please include any SIG/CAIQ that maps to data residency controls.

Appreciate a response by EOD Wednesday (2026-08-25) if possible.

Cheers,
Daniela
Daniela Gomez
Information Security, HavenBank

--
Attachment: (none in initial email)
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Daniela Gomez <daniela.gomez@havenbank.com>
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-20T13:30:00Z
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II report and hosting / dataflow questions

Hi Daniela — thanks for the clear list. Copying our security lead Marissa and account lead Vivek to scope what we can share and to draft a short bridging attestation.

Quick answers up front:
- We can provide the SOC 2 Type II report (redacted where necessary). The current report period ends 2026-03-31.
- We can produce a bridge letter covering controls continuity until contract effective date and will include control owner references.
- For hosted production (Redwood API hosted offering) customer data is processed within EU cloud regions by default when a customer elects EU residency. Control plane metadata (orchestration/telemetry) for some legacy monitoring pipelines may temporarily transit US-based control plane services — we will confirm exact subprocessors and legal basis.

Next steps: Marissa will attach the SOC 2 PDF and the proposed bridge letter draft; Vivek will add any commercial notes. If you want a completed SIG or CAIQ we can start that as well (will take a few days).

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: (none yet)
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Daniela Gomez <daniela.gomez@havenbank.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-21T08:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II report and hosting / dataflow questions

Hi Daniela — attaching the documents below:

Attachments:
- SOC2_TypeII_Report_2025-03.pdf (redacted financials and internal IDs)
- EU_Bridge_Letter_2026-08.pdf (covers control continuity from 2026-04-01 through 2026-09-30)
- dataflow-diagram-eu-us.png (high-level diagram showing control plane vs data plane)

Summary of key points (TL;DR):
- SOC 2 Type II report: audit period 2024-04-01 to 2026-03-31 (testing period). The report attests to our security and availability controls in production for hosted services.
- Bridge letter: confirms controls remained in place after the report period; specifically references encryption at rest/transit, access control, change management, and incident response processes. The bridge will be signed by our Security Lead and Legal.
- Data residency: For customers who select EU residency, the data plane (customer payloads, KV cache used for inference) is served from EU regions only. We provide an option to pin instances to EU-only infrastructure for Dedicated and Private.
- Control plane and telemetry: minimal control-plane metadata (non-sensitive telemetry, job scheduling metadata) may be routed through our global control plane which currently has components in both EU and US regions. We rely on SCCs for cross-border processing of telemetry and monitoring, and maintain a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) referencing SCCs and encryption controls.
- Subprocessors: list in the attached SIG frame (we can provide a redacted version). Key subprocessors: EU cloud region provider (region-specific), monitoring vendor (US-based), backups vendor (EU-based for EU-residency customers).

If you want, we can:
- Provide a redlineable bridge letter for signature by our GC.
- Start a SIG questionnaire and give you the current subprocessor contact list.

Next actions: Daniela — can you confirm whether an attested bridge letter (PDF) is sufficient for procurement, or do you require a Lawyer-signed attestation with SCC references included? Also confirm whether you need the SIG/CAIQ completed before PO issuance.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Security & Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: SOC2_TypeII_Report_2025-03.pdf; EU_Bridge_Letter_2026-08.pdf; dataflow-diagram-eu-us.png
From: Daniela Gomez <daniela.gomez@havenbank.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, security-team@havenbank.com
Date: 2026-08-23T10:20:00Z
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II report and hosting / dataflow questions

Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. A couple of follow-ups:

1) The SOC2 report period noted in your summary seems to mix two dates — can you confirm the testing period start/end in the report header? Procurement requires the tested period explicitly (we need 2025-01-01 through 2026-03-31 to satisfy our policy).
2) Bridge letter: we prefer a Lawyer-signed attestation that calls out SCCs and confirms no backups or cold storage copies of EU-customer payloads are stored in the US without contractual measures. A DPA reference is fine but ideally mention SCC Article numbers.
3) For the control plane telemetry that transits US components, can you provide the minimum dataset that crosses and confirm whether it contains any customer-identifying information? We need that to complete our DPIA.

If you can provide the requested clarifications and an updated bridge letter by EOD Tuesday (2026-08-25) we can move to final legal review.

Regards,
Daniela
From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Daniela Gomez <daniela.gomez@havenbank.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-25T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II report and hosting / dataflow questions

Hi Daniela — quick update from commercial side: we can commit to an EU-only deployment for HavenBank under the Dedicated offering and include an SLA addendum that pins data plane and backups to EU regions. That will remove the need for SCCs for customer data payloads and backups (control plane telemetry exceptions still apply).

Marissa — can you produce the bridge letter revisions Daniela requested and indicate whether the telemetry dataset includes anything PII/PI (we believe it is anonymized job IDs and performance counters only)? Also, please include the SOC2 header exact tested dates in the revised PDF.

Daniela — once we have the revised bridge letter and the final subprocessor list we'll upload a redacted SIG and we can route for legal signoff.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
